checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is the recovered polynomial degree validated before truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff?

reachability.notes: If the recovered polynomial has degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, the truncation discards non-zero coefficients, producing an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_polynomialcoeff function (SG-023) in the codebase. 2. Identify where poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] truncation occurs. 3. Verify there is an explicit check that the polynomial degree is < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB BEFORE truncation. 4. Check if any coefficients at indices >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB could be non-zero after recovery. 5. Analyze the mathematical properties: under what conditions could recovery produce a polynomial with degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB? 6. Craft test input: provide cell data that would cause IFFT to produce coefficients beyond the expected degree. 7. Verify the function either: (a) explicitly checks and rejects such cases, or (b) mathematically guarantees it cannot happen. 8. If relying on mathematical guarantee, verify the assumption is documented and tested.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-18, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Invariant: SG-023:INV-003. Post-condition: truncation must not discard non-zero coefficients.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does the validator node detect and reject incorrect polynomials from recovery?

reachability.notes: If the recovered polynomial has degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, the truncation discards non-zero coefficients, producing an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Trace how the validator node uses the output of recover_polynomialcoeff. 2. Verify the validator performs commitment verification after polynomial recovery. 3. Check if commitment verification would detect an incorrectly truncated polynomial. 4. Verify the validator does not use recovered cells/proofs before commitment verification. 5. Test: provide crafted cells that cause degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, verify the commitment check fails. 6. Ensure error handling: what happens if commitment verification fails? Is the error propagated correctly? 7. Verify the validator does not cache or propagate the incorrect polynomial before verification.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-18, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Covered Node: actor-validator-node. Severity justification: Incorrect truncation produces wrong cells and proofs. However, this should be caught by post-recovery commitment verification.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a P2P peer craft cell data to force polynomial degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB?

reachability.notes: If the recovered polynomial has degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, the truncation discards non-zero coefficients, producing an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Analyze the mathematical relationship between input cells and recovered polynomial degree. 2. Determine if there exist cell values that, when processed through recovery, produce coefficients at indices >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 3. If yes: craft specific test vectors and verify the truncation behavior. 4. Check if the 50% threshold validation (validation_layer) prevents such attacks. 5. Verify the cell availability check (validation_layer) cannot be bypassed. 6. If mathematically impossible to exceed degree, document the proof and ensure it's tested. 7. Consider edge cases: what if exactly 50% of cells are provided? Can attacker choose which cells to maximize degree?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-18, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Covered Node: actor-p2p-peer. Bug bounty notes: Requires demonstrating crafted cell data that causes the recovered polynomial to exceed the expected degree.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is division by zero prevented in recover_polynomialcoeff when computing reconstructed[i] = ez_over_coset[i] / zp_over_coset[i]?

reachability.notes: The coset shift by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY ensures Z(x) has no roots on the coset. If the shift is incorrect, division by zero crashes the node.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_polynomialcoeff function (SG-023) in the codebase. 2. Identify the element-wise division: reconstructed[i] = ez_over_coset[i] / zp_over_coset[i]. 3. Verify zp_over_coset is the vanishing polynomial Z(x) evaluated on the coset. 4. Verify the coset is shifted by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY (the generator of the multiplicative subgroup). 5. Confirm mathematically: Z(x) evaluated at coset points (w * g^i) where w = PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY and g is the FFT root cannot be zero because Z(x) = x^n - 1 has roots at g^i, not at w*g^i. 6. Check the implementation: verify PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is correctly defined and used. 7. Test edge case: what happens if PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is incorrectly set to 1 (no shift)? 8. Verify there are no overflow/underflow issues in the coset shift computation. 9. Check for any code paths that could bypass the coset shift.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-19, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Invariant: SG-023:INV-002. If the coset shift is incorrect, Z(x) evaluates to zero at some points, causing division by zero and node crash.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY correctly defined and verified as a primitive root?

reachability.notes: The coset shift by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY ensures Z(x) has no roots on the coset. If the shift is incorrect, division by zero crashes the node.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the definition of PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY in the codebase. 2. Verify it is a primitive root of unity of the appropriate order (not a root of the FFT domain). 3. Check the mathematical constraint: PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY^n != 1 for any n that divides the FFT domain size. 4. Verify PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is used consistently across all coset operations. 5. Check for any initialization or configuration that could override this value. 6. Verify the value matches the specification (EIP-4844/Danksharding spec). 7. Test: temporarily set PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY to a value that IS a root of the FFT domain, verify this causes division by zero. 8. Ensure there are unit tests validating PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY properties.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-19, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Covered Node: actor-validator-node. The security of the division operation depends entirely on correct coset shift.
